findings.evidence: The only characterization hits are the one-way projections at lines 273 and 286 (`toGroupOfInverse_toSemigroup` and `toGroupOfInverse_reflect_toSemigroup`); no converse theorem occurs in the file.
findings.fix: Add a theorem showing that gluing `U.toSemigroup` and `U.reflect.toSemigroup` recovers `U`, or more generally that any group with forward and reflected semigroups `S` and `T` equals `S.toGroupOfInverse T hST hTS`.
findings.issue: `toGroupOfInverse` has no universal-property or split/glue round-trip theorem, so users cannot identify another group with the glued group without repeating a sign split and extensionality proof.

summary: The gluing constructor exposes its projections but lacks the converse uniqueness/round-trip theorem needed to characterize it as the inverse of splitting a group into its two semigroups.
